source_refs.note: 4. Oil: a main subheading of 33.3 Common Water Pollutants, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 250-250.

blocks.text: Oil pollution in oceans, particularly from oil leaks and spills caused by ships, is a major environmental threat. When oil is accidentally released into the sea, it spreads rapidly across the water surface, forming a layer that blocks sunlight and reduces oxygen exchange. This severely harms marine life, including fish, birds, and mammals. Marine mammals can ingest the toxic oil while grooming, and fish may suffer from long-term health issues due to exposure to hydrocarbons. Oil pollution also damages coastal habitats such as mangroves, coral reefs, and beaches.
